points: This time the message is visual: Yirmiyahu wears a loincloth and never washes it, until it is filthy.
The message: you were meant to cling to Hashem, but you got dirty and never cleaned up. Yom Kippur is a deep clean, and they never stopped for one.

He buries it by the Peras, hinting at Bavel, or, some say, on the road to Mitzrayim, showing the people sliding back to Egyptian ways. He also tells the king (Yehoyachin) and his mother to stop being so arrogant.
"B'mistarim tivkeh nafshi": either Yirmiyahu crying in secret, or, per the Midrash, Hashem Himself crying as He punishes us. He wants us close.
The Ramban: a navi's small actions make the message real in this world. Rav Kook: even a small thought of teshuvah changes reality, so don't dismiss it.
